h1: The 6 Best Leaf Blowers for Wet Leaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Leaf Blowers for Wet Leaves: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six leaf blowers with the highest listed airflow for heavy, damp leaf piles, from gas backpack units to cordless handhelds.
summary: The EGO Power+ Cordless at 880 CFM is our top pick, because it pairs high listed airflow with battery convenience. The Echo X Series backpack tops the chart at 1110 CFM for large properties. The PROYAMA 72cc gas backpack matches the EGO on airflow for a lower price bucket, and the LOSART is the cheapest cordless entry.
intro: Wet leaves are heavy, and a blower that handles dry piles can simply skate across a soggy lawn. When leaves are packed together and damp, the number to read on the listing is CFM, the volume of air the machine moves, rather than the miles per hour in the headline.

We reviewed leaf blowers by their listed airflow and ranked six. No listing here promises wet-leaf results, so the ranking assumes what is plain physics from the specs: more stated CFM means more air behind each push, at the cost of weight, noise or price.

products.name: EGO Power+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 880 CFM in a handheld cordless body.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ is a handheld cordless electric blower with a listed 880 CFM. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It leads because 880 CFM without a fuel tank is the best mix of power and convenience here. The Echo above it in raw numbers is gas and costs far more.

It suits homeowners who want strong airflow without gas. Check that the battery is included before you buy.
products.skipIf: You maintain acres and want gas.

products.name: Echo 220 MPH 1110 CFM 79.9 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Backpack Blower
products.verdict: The highest listed airflow here, at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH.
products.description:
The Echo X Series is a 79.9 cc gas 2-stroke backpack blower listed at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH. It is in the $500+ bucket, the highest here.

It takes second place because the cost jump is steep for the extra airflow over the EGO, and a backpack gas unit is heavier to carry.

It is built for large properties with heavy leaf cover. Plan on fuel mixing and noise.
products.idealFor: Large properties with heavy leaf cover.

products.name: PROYAMA 72CC Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 880 CFM from a 72cc gas backpack in a lower bucket.
products.description:
The PROYAMA is a 72 cc gas backpack blower listed at 880 CFM. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It lands third because it equals the EGO on listed airflow for a lower bucket, but it is gas powered and carried on the back.

A match for owners who want the cheapest 880 CFM. Expect to handle fuel.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 765 CFM gas backpack from a named outdoor brand.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 150BT is a gas backpack blower listed at 765 CFM. It is in the $200-500 bucket.

Fourth spot reflects lower listed airflow than the PROYAMA at a higher bucket, offset by the maker's name.

It suits buyers who prefer an established maker. Compare it with the PROYAMA on price.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer an established brand.
products.skipIf: You want the most airflow per dollar.

products.name: MTKOALA Leaf Blower Cordless
products.verdict: A handheld cordless blower listed at 700 CFM.
products.description:
The MTKOALA is a handheld cordless blower listed at 700 CFM. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It places fifth because its airflow is lower than the EGO and its bucket is cheaper, so it fills the gap in between.

It works for suburban lots. Confirm the battery and charger are in the box.
products.idealFor: Suburban lots with a cordless preference.
products.skipIf: You face very heavy leaf piles.

products.name: LOSART Leaf Blower Cordless
products.verdict: A 650 CFM cordless blower in a low bucket.
products.description:
The LOSART is a cordless blower listed at 650 CFM. It is in the $50-100 bucket.

It closes the list with the lowest airflow here but also among the lowest prices.

It suits small yards and light damp cleanup. Expect to work in smaller piles.
products.skipIf: You need to move heavy piles.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is cubic feet of air per minute, the volume the blower moves. Heavy damp piles need volume to shift, so it matters more than top speed. Find the CFM number in the title or bullets.
MPH is air speed at the nozzle. It helps lift stuck leaves but does not move a pile alone. Use it as a tie-breaker, as on the Echo's 220 MPH.
Gas gives long runtime and big airflow but needs fuel and noise tolerance. Cordless is quieter and simpler but limited by battery. Check what is in the box.
A backpack spreads the weight, which suits long sessions. Handhelds are lighter for short jobs. Match the style to the yard size.
A listing with no CFM is hard to compare. Treat that gap with caution, as with the Husqvarna 360BT we left out.

howToChoose.intro: Bigger yards need more air and a comfortable carry.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: More airflow and runtime, with fuel and noise. The Echo X Series, PROYAMA and Husqvarna 150BT are gas.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Quieter and simpler. The EGO Power+, MTKOALA and LOSART are cordless.

howToChoose.note: Most homeowners should go cordless unless the property is large.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: The highest stated CFM you can carry and afford.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The EGO Power+ lists 880 CFM and the Echo X Series lists 1110 CFM.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clear large lots, where the Echo X Series earns its bucket.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your yard is small, so the LOSART is enough.

faq.q: What CFM do I need for wet leaves?
faq.a: No listing gives a wet-leaf figure, so go for the highest stated CFM within your budget.
Buying on MPH alone. Airflow volume does more work on heavy piles.

faq.q: Is the Echo worth it over the EGO?
faq.a: Only on large properties. For most yards the EGO costs far less.

faq.q: How do I start a gas backpack?
faq.a: Mix fuel as the manual directs and follow the start steps. Do not guess the ratio.
Keep air filters clean and store with the fuel plan from the manual.

faq.q: Can a cordless blower handle wet piles?
faq.a: The EGO lists 880 CFM, so on paper it can, but expect shorter runtime.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ is the best fit for most yards. Step up to the Echo X Series only for big properties, and use the PROYAMA if you want gas airflow for less. Whichever you buy, read the CFM first.
